v.en: O God, come to my assistance;

r.la: Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
r.en: And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

full.en: The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.

la: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
en: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

v.en: Let them know that the Lord is thy name.

r.la: Tu solus Altíssimus super omnem terram.
r.en: Thou alone art the most High over all the earth.

text.la: Suscitávit Dóminus * testimónium in Iacob: et legem pósuit in Israël.
text.en: The Lord set up a testimony in Jacob: * and made a law in Israel.

text.la: Coram pátribus eórum * fecit Deus mirabília.
text.en: The Lord did wonderful things * in the sight of their fathers.

text.la: Iánuas cæli apéruit * Dóminus, et pluit illis manna ad manducándum.
text.en: The Lord opened * the doors of heaven and had rained down manna upon them to eat.

text.la: Deus adiútor * est eórum: et Excélsus redémptor eórum est.
text.en: God is their helper, * and the most high God their redeemer.

text.la: Redémit eos * Dóminus de manu tribulántis.
text.en: The Lord redeemed them * from the hand of him that afflicted them.

text.la: Ædificávit * Deus sanctifícium suum in terra.
text.en: God built * his sanctuary in the earth.

text.la: Ádiuva nos, * Deus, salutáris noster: et propítius esto peccátis nostris.
text.en: Help us, O God, our Saviour, * deliver us: and forgive us our sins.

text.la: Ego sum Dóminus * Deus tuus Israël, qui edúxi te de terra Ægýpti.
text.en: I am the Lord * God of Israel, who brought you out from the land of Egypt.

text.la: Ne táceas Deus * quóniam inimíci tui extulérunt caput.
text.en: Be not thou silent, O Lord, * for Thy enemies lifted up their head.

text.la: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
text.en: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

text.la: Ipsíus píetas et misericórdia nos ádiuvet, qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivit et regnat in sǽcula sæculórum.
text.en: May His loving-kindness and mercy help us, Who liveth and reigneth with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, world without end.

benedictio.la: Deus Pater omnípotens sit nobis propítius et clemens.
benedictio.en: May God the Father Omnipotent, be to us merciful and clement.

source.en: Lesson from the book of Ecclesiasticus

text.la: 1 Fili, peccásti? non adícias íterum, sed et de prístinis deprecáre, ut tibi dimittántur. 2 Quasi a fácie cólubri fuge peccáta et, si accésseris ad illa, suscípient te. 3 Dentes leónis dentes eius interficiéntes ánimas hóminum, 4 Quasi rhomphǽa bis acúta omnis iníquitas, plagæ illíus non est sánitas. 5 Obiurgátio et iniúriæ annullábunt substántiam, et domus quæ nimis lócuples est, annullábitur supérbia: sic substántia supérbi eradicábitur.
text.en: 1 My son, hast thou sinned? do so no more: but for thy former sins also pray that they may be forgiven thee. 2 Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest near them, they will take hold of thee. 3 The teeth thereof are the teeth of a lion, killing the souls of men. 4 All iniquity is like a two-edged sword, there is no remedy for the wound thereof. 5 Injuries and wrongs will waste riches: and the house that is very rich shall be brought to nothing by pride: so the substance of the proud shall be rooted out.

body.la: Da mihi, Dómine, sédium tuárum assistrícem sapiéntiam, et noli me reprobáre a púeris tuis:
body.en: Give me wisdom, O Lord, that sitteth by thy throne, and reject me not from among thy children.

refrain.la: Quóniam servus tuus sum ego, et fílius ancíllæ tuæ.
refrain.en: For I am thy servant and son of thine handmaid.

verse.la: Mitte illam de sede magnitúdinis tuæ, ut mecum sit et mecum labóret.
verse.en: O send her out from the throne of thy glory, to be with me and to labour with me.

benedictio.la: Christus perpétuæ det nobis gáudia vitæ.
benedictio.en: May Christ to all His people give, for ever in His sight to live.

text.la: 6 Deprecátio páuperis ex ore usque ad aures eius pervéniet, et iudícium festináto advéniet illi. 7 Qui odit correptiónem, vestígium est peccatóris; et, qui timet Deum, convertétur ad cor suum. 8 Notus a longe potens lingua audáci, et sensátus scit labi se ab ipso. 9 Qui ædíficat domum suam impéndiis aliénis, quasi qui cólligit lápides suos in híeme. 10 Stuppa collécta synagóga peccántium, et consummátio illórum flamma ignis.
text.en: 6 The prayer out of the mouth of the poor shall reach the ears of God, and judgment shall come for him speedily. 7 He that hateth to be reproved walketh in the trace of a sinner: and he that feareth God will turn to his own heart. 8 He that is mighty by a bold tongue is known afar off, but a wise man knoweth to slip by him. 9 He that buildeth his house at other men's charges, is as he that gathereth himself stones to build in the winter. 10 The congregation of sinners is like tow heaped together, and the end of them is a flame of fire.

body.en: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

refrain.la: Intelléctus bonus ómnibus faciéntibus eum: laudátio eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
refrain.en: A good understanding have all they that do His commandments. His praise endureth for ever.

verse.la: Diléctio illíus custódia legum est: quia omnis sapiéntia timor Dómini.
verse.en: Love is the keeping of her laws, for all wisdom is the fear of the Lord.

benedictio.la: Ignem sui amóris accéndat Deus in córdibus nostris.
benedictio.en: May the Spirit's fire Divine in our hearts enkindled shine.

text.la: 11 Via peccántium complanáta lapídibus, et in fine illórum ínferi et ténebræ et pœnæ. 12 Qui custódit iustítiam, continébit sensum eius. 13 Consummátio timóris Dei, sapiéntia et sensus. 14 Non erudiétur qui non est sápiens in bono; 15 Est autem sapiéntia quæ abúndat in malo, et non est sensus ubi est amaritúdo. 16 Sciéntia sapiéntis tamquam inundátio abundábit, et consílium illíus sicut fons vitæ pérmanet.
text.en: 11 The way of sinners is made plain with stones, and in their end is hell, and darkness, and pains. 12 He that keepeth justice shall get the understanding thereof. 13 The perfection of the fear of God is wisdom and understanding. 14 He that is not wise in good, will not be taught. 15 But there is a wisdom that aboundeth in evil: and there is no understanding where there is bitterness. 16 The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood, and his counsel continueth like a fountain of life

body.la: Verbum iníquum et dolósum longe fac a me, Dómine:
body.en: Lord, remove far from me vanity and lies.

refrain.la: Divítias et paupertátem ne déderis mihi, sed tantum víctui meo tríbue necessária.
refrain.en: Give me neither poverty nor riches, but feed me with food convenient for me.

verse.la: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
verse.en: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

text.la: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi Laudes separandæ sint.
text.en: Skip the rest, unless praying Lauds separately.

text.la: Custódi, Dómine, quǽsumus, Ecclésiam tuam propitiatióne perpétua: et quia sine te lábitur humána mortálitas; tuis semper auxíliis et abstrahátur a nóxiis et ad salutária dirigátur.
text.en: Keep, we beseech thee, O Lord, thy Church with thy perpetual mercy, and because the frailty of man without thee cannot but fall, keep us ever by thy help from all things hurtful, and lead us to all things profitable to our salvation.

office.title: Feria Sexta infra Hebd XIV post Octavam Pentecostes V. Augusti
